result:
Solution 1 is wrong. It claims 14400, the Hill number H(33), is achievable by a pseudolinear drawing. But pseudolinear (and rectilinear) drawings cannot reach the Hill value for large n. For comparison, the rectilinear crossing number of K₃₀ is 9726, above H(30) = 9555. For K₃₃ the pseudolinear minimum should therefore lie strictly above 14400, probably around 15,000. Its j-edge arithmetic also does not hold up.

Solution 2 is wrong. It counts all 4-orbit selections as crossings, giving 26730, which is far more than the roughly 0.38·C(33,4) ≈ 15,500 crossings of typical good drawings. That count is too large to be a minimum.

Solution 3 gives 15834, which is divisible by 3 and lies in the plausible range for a 3-symmetric pseudolinear minimum, above the unsymmetric value. Its derivation is vague, but its final number is the only one consistent with the expected range. I could not verify it independently.

CHOICE: 3
